title: The Thorn of Ashvale Anew
premise: Isandro Delacroix, youngest and least regarded member of the Ashvale Wardens—a guild sworn to keep magic out of the valley where it cannot follow—finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies hidden in the guild vault. The prophecy names her as the one who must reforge the broken covenant between the valley and the magical realm beyond its borders before the moon completes its thirteenth turn, or both realms will wither. As she journeys beyond the valley for the first time, Isandro discovers that the guild's founders deliberately shattered the covenant and erased the memory of why, sacrificing the outer realm to keep their own safe. Torn between loyalty to the only family she has ever known and the truth of what they did, she must choose justice outside the law: in the climax she reforges the covenant by willingly surrendering her own memories of Ashvale as the price, letting magic flow back into the valley while carrying nothing of her old life forward—except a single thorn pressed in wax, which in the final chapter blooms into recognition when an old friend finds her anew.
about_author: Felix Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken oaths in municipal records before turning to fantasy. They write in a converted chapel in the north of England, where they keep a garden that stubbornly refuses to grow anything but thorns.

chapters.title: The Date That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. During a routine inventory of the Warden vault, Isandro finds a prophecy book whose final entry bears tomorrow's date—and her name. Her hands shake as she hides it from the guildmaster. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath the tedium of a small, safe life about to crack open.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She tests the prophecy against guild law and learns the valley's boundary stones are not protection but a seal—one side of a covenant 'paused,' not ended. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing her whole world is a locked room.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Kindness
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Veyra's POV. Veyra discovers Isandro's snooping but responds with unexpected warmth, assigning her to archive duty instead of punishment. Isandro can't tell if it's mercy or surveillance. Emotional beat: loyalty offered like a leash.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cross-referencing lunar records, she confirms the moon completes its thirteenth turn in under a year—the deadline. A dying elder Warden whispers that the last person named in the book never came home. Emotional beat: the clock begins.

chapters.title: The Boundary Stones
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At night she walks the perimeter and touches a stone; it burns cold and shows her a flash of another sky. Her friend Tam follows her out and, instead of reporting her, asks to come along. Emotional beat: first act of chosen loyalty.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The two slip past the stones at moonrise. Magic floods back into them like blood into a numb limb—Tam weeps at colors he has no names for. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by guilt at what they've abandoned.

chapters.title: The Withered Realm
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Beyond the border lies a land slowly dying without the covenant's flow: gray orchards, silent shrines, refugees who flinch at the sight of valley steel. Emotional beat: horror at learning her safety was purchased with someone else's slow starvation.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Sable Hollow
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A blind archivist named Ondine recognizes the Delacroix name and reveals Isandro's grandmother was the last Warden to cross over—and was erased from all records. Emotional beat: grief for a family tree cut down on purpose.

chapters.title: The First Shard
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The covenant can be reforged only by uniting three shards of the original oath-stone, held by three estranged heirs. The first heir, a river-ferryman, agrees to help—but demands Isandro swear the truth will be told publicly in Ashvale. Emotional beat: the cost of promises made aloud.

chapters.title: Letters Home
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A smuggled letter arrives from Veyra: come home, say nothing, all is forgiven. Isandro realizes the guild knows exactly where she is. Emotional beat: love weaponized; the ache of being missed and managed at once.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Refused
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The second shard's keeper, a war-scarred knight, hates the valley and refuses to even hear Isandro out until she stands witness to a memorial for those who died in the realm's decline. Emotional beat: justice demanded before trust granted.

chapters.title: Veyra's Version
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Interlude revealing the guildmaster's history: she crossed over young, saw the realm's suffering, and chose the valley anyway because saving everyone was impossible. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; conviction that feels like virtue from inside.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Shrine
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Guild wardens sent to retrieve Isandro ambush the group; Tam takes a wound meant for her, and the second shard is nearly lost. Isandro uses forbidden valley craft to drive them off. Emotional beat: the moment she stops being able to go back unchanged.

chapters.title: Memory Is a Country
chapters.summary: Ondine's POV. The archivist explains the covenant's true price: whoever reforges it must pay with their memories of the life they're binding it to. The founders refused to pay, so they broke it instead. Emotional beat: understanding the full weight of the choice ahead.

chapters.title: What Tam Saw
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Recovering, Tam confesses he originally followed Isandro under orders from Veyra—but chose her instead. Isandro must decide whether his loyalty, born of betrayal, can be trusted. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth colliding inside a friendship.

chapters.title: The Third Keeper
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The third shard rests in Ashvale itself, in the guild vault where the prophecy was found. To get it, Isandro must walk back through the front door and face everyone she lied to. Emotional beat: dread braided with homesickness.

chapters.title: Return of the Prodigal Liar
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Confrontation in the guild hall: Veyra offers Isandro the shard freely if she'll renounce the quest and let the realms stay divided. Isandro refuses—not with anger, but with testimony, naming the dead of the outer realm aloud. Emotional beat: truth spoken to power at personal ruin.

chapters.title: The Vault of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. When negotiation fails, Tam steals the third shard during the chaos of a guild schism—old wardens splitting between Veyra's law and Isandro's cause. Emotional beat: the thief's terror and strange exhilaration; the guild breaking along its oldest fault line.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Pursued by loyalist wardens, the trio races the shards to the boundary stones as the thirteenth moon rises. Veyra herself blocks the path, blade drawn, tears on her face. Emotional beat: everything converging; no clean exits left.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax. At the stones, Isandro joins the three shards and speaks the covenant whole, offering her memories of Ashvale as payment. Veyra, at the last, lowers her blade and adds her own hand to the rite. Magic floods the valley as Isandro's past dissolves. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship—she chooses who she'll be by choosing what she'll lose.

chapters.title: A Valley That Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Aftermath: green returns to the withered realm, wardens begin public reckoning with their founders' crime, and Veyra resigns rather than preside over a guild built on erasure. Isandro wakes in Ashvale knowing no one, tended by strangers who owe her everything. Emotional beat: bittersweet dawn; justice achieved at the price of self.

chapters.title: The Thorn in Bloom
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Months later, living quietly in the changed valley, Isandro finds a pressed thorn in her pocket she cannot explain. Tam approaches her in the market, introduces himself, and begins again—telling her, patiently, the story of who she was. Emotional beat: resolution as renewal; memory lost but loyalty, freely given twice, endures.
